panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: Streaming HTTP measurements are collected on the benchmark node against its temporary loopback llama-server. They include local client overhead and server waiting, but not a remote user’s network latency. Successful-request distributions are provisional during measurement; always inspect failures and sample counts. **Tail percentiles from fewer than 100 successes are descriptive, not reliable production p99 estimates.** Choose the case/stage series of interest; earlier cases retain their final observations until another experiment starts.

options.content: Streaming HTTP measurements are collected on the benchmark node against its temporary loopback llama-server. They include local client overhead and server waiting, but not a remote user’s network latency. Successful-request distributions are provisional during measurement; always inspect failures and sample counts. **Tail percentiles from fewer than 100 successes are descriptive, not reliable production p99 estimates.** Choose the case/stage series of interest; earlier cases retain their final observations until another experiment starts. Resource observation starts before warmup, spans stage transitions and continues after completion for one minute after measurement. Final model results remain fixed; node resources keep updating. The CLI opens a start-anchored time range, preserved by dashboard links.

panels.title: End-to-end request latency
panels.description: Request dispatch to terminal response. Lower means the complete answer is available sooner. A 2-second TTFT plus 10 seconds of output still gives roughly 12 seconds total; compare equal input/output workloads. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

targets.expr: ((modelgauge_live_value{stage=~"$stage",case=~"$case",measurement=~"latency_ms_(mean|p50|p90|p95|p99|max)"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{stage=~"$stage",case=~"$case",measurement=~"latency_ms_(mean|p50|p90|p95|p99|max)"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) and (timestamp((modelgauge_live_value{stage=~"$stage",case=~"$case",measurement=~"latency_ms_(mean|p50|p90|p95|p99|max)"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{stage=~"$stage",case=~"$case",measurement=~"latency_ms_(mean|p50|p90|p95|p99|max)"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) <= scalar(modelgauge_live_window_end_seconds @ end()))

Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

panels.title: Time per output token (TPOT)
panels.description: Average milliseconds per output token after the first: (last output event − TTFT)/(output tokens − 1). Lower is faster. 50 ms/token corresponds to roughly 20 tokens/s after startup. Requires valid token accounting. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

panels.description: Completed successful requests per second and successful requests meeting configured targets/output checks per second. Use goodput for latency-constrained capacity; missing goodput means targets were absent or not fully evaluable. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

panels.description: Accounted successful input/output tokens per elapsed second across all concurrent requests. Higher means more combined capacity, not necessarily faster output for each user. Input rate includes the full request lifecycle. Unavailable unless all successes report token usage. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

panels.title: Request outcomes
panels.description: Case counts: offered work, dispatched work, successes and outcomes. Timeouts/incomplete responses also contribute to errors, so categories are not all additive. Client-capacity drops are requests never sent, not server rejections. Expected cancellation probes should be interpreted separately. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

A configured output cap is often intentional; this is not automatically a failure. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. panels.description: 1 means the post-load/cancellation request succeeded; 0 means it failed. Missing means the case has no probe or it has not run yet. This tests service usability, not benchmark job recovery. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final.
